raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This PR adds `--data-parallel-lb-policy` to the internal DP load balancer.
- `requests` is the default and keeps today's routing.
- `tokens` and `dualpath` also count each engine's tokens, not just its requests.
- `dualpath` follows the decode-engine scheduler of [DualPath](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.21548) and balances tokens and requests together.

**Status: closed.** On the two models tested on 8x H200, neither token-aware policy gives a consistent end-to-end gain. See Results.

## Claims

- With DP attention + EP, the ranks step in lockstep, so the slowest rank sets every step. A rank's request count sets its batch size, and its tokens set its attention cost (full attention, MLA, DSA indexer/top-k, compressed attention). When request lengths vary widely, balancing request counts alone can leave some ranks with much more attention work than others. `dualpath` balances both.
- `--data-parallel-lb-policy requests` (the default) keeps today's routing. Unless a token-aware policy is selected, engines skip the token sum and the front-end skips the token bookkeeping.
- End-to-end effect on 8x H200: no consistent gain.
  - `dualpath` stays within run-to-run noise of `requests`, except +2-3% throughput at C=64/128 on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017.
  - `tokens` alone loses up to 9%.

## Results

**Setup.**
- 8x H200, DP8 + EP8, `DecodeBenchConnector`, `vllm-rs bench serve` with prompt token IDs.
- Workload: ISL ~ U[1.3K, 261K], OSL 512, N = 4 x C.
- All three policies run on one server with the same request sequence in each pass. The policy order rotates per pass, and there are 3 passes.
- KV cache is not full, except where noted.

Output throughput relative to `requests`, median [min, max] over the 3 passes:

| Model | C | `tokens` | `dualpath` |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (DSpark, 3 draft tokens, synthetic acceptance) | 64 | 0.967 [0.966, 1.028] | 1.028 [1.001, 1.035] |
| | 128 | 0.935 [0.932, 0.967] | 1.020 [1.015, 1.032] |
| | 256 | 1.011 [1.003, 1.059] | 1.062 [0.979, 1.067] |
| | 384 | 0.962 [0.949, 0.985] | 0.971 [0.933, 1.038] |
| | 512 | 0.913 [0.896, 0.952] | 0.989 [0.971, 1.008] |
| GLM-5.3-Flash (MTP, 3 draft tokens, synthetic acceptance) | 64 | 0.927 [0.883, 0.946] | 1.006 [0.973, 1.020] |
| | 128 | 0.999 [0.970, 1.001] | 0.999 [0.955, 1.060] |
| | 192 | 0.998 [0.941, 1.007] | 0.973 [0.956, 1.001] |

GLM-5.3-Flash at C >= 224 hits KV capacity (waiting requests, preemptions). There, every policy varies by up to +/-50% from run to run, so those rows are left out.

**Why the gain is small.**
- `dualpath` does even out per-rank context tokens. On V4.1 at C=64, the coordinator snapshots show max/mean per-rank tokens drop from 1.41 to 1.27 (median).
- But both models' decode step depends little on context length.
  - On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 with equal per-rank load (fixed ISL, C=256, `requests`), TPOT p50 is 24.5 / 23.8 / 24.4 / 28.4 ms at 4K / 64K / 128K / 256K.
  - GLM-5.3-Flash is mostly linear attention.
- So balancing context tokens can only recover a few percent of the slowest rank's step.

**`tokens` alone is worse than `requests`.**
- It skews request counts across ranks, and with them batch sizes. On V4.1 at C=64, per-rank running max/mean is 1.40, against 1.16 for `requests`.
- At the `--max-num-seqs` limit (V4.1, C=512, 64 per rank), it also queues requests on full ranks: mean waiting is 17.6 vs 9.6, and p99 TTFT is +21%.
- `dualpath` avoids both.

<details>
<summary>Commands and measured code</summary>

Measured code:
- vLLM main fa75d345 with this PR's routing changes ported onto it.
- Plus #61566 and #56082 (RecoverSSM, used by the GLM-5.3-Flash runs).
- Plus an experiment-only hook that re-reads the policy from a file, so that all three policies share one server. A coordinator snapshot log records per-engine `[waiting, running, kv_cache_usage, num_kv_tokens]`.

Server (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017):

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 \
  --data-parallel-size 8 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-num-seqs 64 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"DecodeBenchConnector","kv_role":"kv_both"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":3,"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_rates":[0.8,0.6,0.5]}'
```

GLM-5.3-Flash uses the same flags, with two changes:
- `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp",...}'` (same synthetic rates)
- `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}' --use-replayssm`

Client, per pass `P` (seed) and concurrency `C`:

```bash
vllm-rs bench serve --backend vllm --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 131072 --random-output-len 512 \
  --random-range-ratio '{"input": 0.99, "output": 0.0}' \
  --prompt-token-ids --ignore-eos --request-rate inf \
  --max-concurrency $C --num-prompts $((4 * C)) --seed $P
```

Fixed-ISL sensitivity: the same client with `--random-input-len {4096,65536,131072,262144}`, `--random-range-ratio '{"input": 0.0, "output": 0.0}'` and C=256, on the `requests` policy.

</details>

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass, mypy included.
- Unit tests: `pytest tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core_client.py -k dplb`: 16 passed.
  - This needs a one-line test-helper fix that is not pushed, since the PR is closed: `_make_dplb_client` must build four-field load entries.
- E2E benchmarks: see Results.
- Model evaluation: not applicable. The policy only changes which DP engine runs a request; outputs are unchanged.

## Details

**Policy (`dualpath`).** For a request with `n` prompt tokens, let `tok_e` and `req_e` be engine `e`'s token and request loads.
- Engines with a KV-bound waiting queue are skipped unless every engine has one. A KV-bound queue means waiting requests at >= 50% KV usage, the same signal the default policy already penalizes.
- With `Z = 1.05 * (sum_e tok_e + n) / E`:
  - if some engines satisfy `tok_e + n <= Z`, choose the one among them with the fewest requests;
  - otherwise, choose the engine with the fewest tokens.

Short requests therefore fill request-count gaps on token-heavy engines, and long requests go to token-light engines. DualPath additionally checks free HBM per engine; here the KV-bound-queue check stands in for it.

**Load estimate.** As for request counts today, each engine's load is the larger of the coordinator's latest snapshot and this client's in-flight load times `client_count`. The client also counts each routed request locally until the next snapshot.

**Plumbing.** `SchedulerStats.num_kv_tokens` (tokens of waiting + running requests) is published with the existing DP LB stats.
- It is computed only when a token-aware policy is selected, and only when request counts change, so the publish cadence is unchanged.
- The coordinator snapshot grows from 3 to 4 fields per engine.

**Why this is not a duplicate.**
- #40795 (token-level LB for prefill-heavy load, closed for inactivity) scored `waiting_tokens * 4 + running_tokens`. That is close to `tokens` here. `tokens` alone balances tokens but can skew request counts, and with them batch sizes; `dualpath` balances both.
- #58070 / #61386 add result-metric signals (queue time, preemptions), #43279 adds power-of-two-choices sampling, and #43483 / #52464 route for prefix-cache hits. These are orthogonal. #61386 also widens the coordinator snapshot, so the two changes would need a rebase against each other.
- SGLang has `--load-balance-method total_tokens` (fewest tokens). There is no DualPath-style two-dimensional policy in SGLang or vLLM.

**Limitations.**
- The Rust front-end (`VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`) keeps request-count routing; a port would be a follow-up.
- External LB mode is unaffected, since vLLM does not route between ranks there.
- Token growth during decode is reflected at the next request-count change, not every step.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.

nodes.body: Closing this. On the two models I could test on 8x H200, the token-aware policies give no consistent end-to-end gain; the description has the numbers. The decode step of these models depends little on context length, which caps what token balancing can recover. The branch stays available for anyone who wants to retry on a model whose decode cost grows with context length, or at wider DP.

@@ -74,7 +74,7 @@ There are several notable differences when using Ray:
 - When a single DP group requires multiple nodes, *e.g.* in case a single model replica needs to run on at least two nodes, make sure to set `VLLM_RAY_DP_PACK_STRATEGY="span"` in which case `--data-parallel-size-local` is ignored and will be automatically determined
 - Remote DP ranks will be allocated based on node resources of the Ray cluster
 
-Currently, the internal DP load balancing is done within the API server process(es) and is based on the running and waiting queues in each of the engines. This could be made more sophisticated in future by incorporating KV cache aware logic.
+The internal DP load balancing is done within the API server process(es). By default it is based on the running and waiting queues in each of the engines. `--data-parallel-lb-policy` selects a token-aware alternative: `tokens` sends each request to the engine holding the fewest tokens, and `dualpath` balances tokens and request counts together, following the decode-engine scheduler of [DualPath](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.21548). With DP attention and expert parallelism the ranks step in lockstep, so the slowest rank sets every step: its request count sets the batch size and its tokens set the attention cost. When request lengths vary widely, balancing request counts alone can leave one rank with far more attention work than the others.
 
 When deploying large DP sizes using this method, the API server process can become a bottleneck. In this case, the orthogonal `--api-server-count` command line option can be used to scale this out (for example `--api-server-count=4`). This is transparent to users - a single HTTP endpoint / port is still exposed. Note that this API server scale-out is "internal" and still confined to the "head" node.

+    engine = client.get_core_engine_for_request(request)
+    assert client.engine_inflight_tokens[engine] == 7

+_KV_BOUND_USAGE = 0.5

+    """Pick an engine for a request under a token-aware DP LB policy.

+    Args:
+        policy: "tokens" or "dualpath".

+            tuple per engine, in scan order; ties go to the earliest entry.
+        num_tokens: tokens the new request brings.
+
+    Returns:
+        The index into `loads` of the chosen engine.
+
+    """
+    indices = range(len(loads))
+    if policy == "tokens":
+        return min(indices, key=lambda i: (loads[i][1], loads[i][0]))
+    assert policy == "dualpath", policy

issue_comments.body: Closing this. On the two models I could test on 8x H200, the token-aware policies give no consistent end-to-end gain; the description has the numbers. The decode step of these models depends little on context length, which caps what token balancing can recover. The branch stays available for anyone who wants to retry on a model whose decode cost grows with context length, or at wider DP.
